usage: Everyday request at a desk or counter; 좀 softens it
Please write with a black pen
Banks/offices often require 검은색 (black); 으로 marks the tool
안 나오다 = ink won't come out; the standard way to say a pen is dead
Casual workplace ask; drop the subject marker in speech
examples: 서류에 볼펜으로 서명하시면 됩니다.
You can sign the document with a pen.
Common at banks and government offices; 으로 = with/using
볼펜 잉크가 다 떨어져서 새로 샀어요.
The pen ran out of ink, so I bought a new one.
잉크가 떨어지다 = run out of ink
회의 때 쓸 볼펜이 한 자루도 없네요.
There isn't a single pen to use in the meeting.
자루 is the counter for pens; 한 자루도 없다 = not even one
nuance: 볼펜 specifically means a ballpoint pen, while 펜 is the generic word for any pen. In daily life Koreans say 볼펜 by default for the cheap office pens, and reserve 사인펜 (felt-tip) or 만년필 (fountain pen) for those specific types.
mistakes: Saying 볼펜이 안 써져요 sounds slightly off; native speakers say 볼펜이 안 나와요 for a dead pen
Counting pens with 개 instead of the more natural 자루 in writing

usage: Jot it down in your notebook
적어 두다 = write down and keep; common note-taking phrase
Can you show me your notes?
필기 = handwritten notes; casual peer request
권 is the counter for books/notebooks
정리 = organizing; compliment about tidy notes
examples: 회의 내용을 노트에 다 적었어요.
I wrote down everything from the meeting in my notebook.
Practical for work; 노트 here is a physical pad
노트 한 권을 거의 다 썼어요.
I've used up almost a whole notebook.
다 쓰다 = use up completely
디지털 노트보다 종이 노트가 더 편해요.
I find a paper notebook more comfortable than a digital one.
Contrasts 종이 (paper) vs 디지털; common preference talk
nuance: 노트 means a paper notebook for jotting things down; be careful not to confuse it with 노트북, which always means a laptop computer in Korean. Older textbooks taught 공책 for a school notebook, but adults overwhelmingly say 노트 in daily and office life.
mistakes: Using 노트북 when you mean a paper notebook — that word means laptop
Counting notebooks with 개 instead of the natural 권

usage: Please stick it down with tape
로 marks the tool; 붙이다 = to stick
박스테이프 = the wide brown packing tape, super common when moving
The tape won't come off easily
안 떨어지다 = won't come off; common complaint
I fixed it with clear tape
examples: 택배 상자를 테이프로 단단히 붙였어요.
I sealed the delivery box tightly with tape.
Everyday when shipping/moving; 단단히 = firmly
벽에 포스터를 테이프로 붙여도 될까요?
May I put the poster on the wall with tape?
Polite permission with -아/어도 될까요?
양면테이프가 일반 테이프보다 훨씬 잘 붙어요.
Double-sided tape sticks much better than regular tape.
양면테이프 = double-sided tape; 훨씬 = much more
nuance: 테이프 covers most sticky tapes, but Koreans usually specify the type: 박스테이프 (packing), 투명 테이프 or 스카치테이프 (clear desk tape), and 양면테이프 (double-sided). The verb 붙이다 (to stick something) is what you pair with it, not 붙다 (to be stuck).
mistakes: Saying 테이프를 붙다 — use the transitive 붙이다 since you are sticking something
Calling clear desk tape 박스테이프; that wide brown tape is only for boxes

usage: 찍다 is the verb for stapling; 로 marks the tool
심 = the staple refills; 떨어지다 = run out
두 장 = two sheets; 장 counts paper
Polite borrowing in a shared office
examples: 보고서를 출력해서 스테이플러로 찍었어요.
I printed the report and stapled it.
Typical office flow; 출력하다 = to print out
스테이플러 심이 없어서 클립으로 묶었어요.
There were no staples, so I held it together with a clip.
Links to 심 and 클립; 묶다 = bind
스테이플러가 자꾸 걸려서 잘 안 찍혀요.
The stapler keeps jamming, so it doesn't staple well.
걸리다 = to jam/catch; 찍히다 = to get stapled
nuance: The native verb for using a stapler is 찍다 (literally to stamp/punch), so '스테이플러로 찍다' is the natural collocation rather than any borrowed verb. The staple refills are called 스테이플러 심 or just 심, the same word used for pencil lead and refill cartridges.
mistakes: Saying 스테이플러하다 as a verb — there is no such verb; use 스테이플러로 찍다
Calling the refills 스테이플 instead of the everyday 심

usage: I wrote a memo on a Post-it and stuck it up
메모하다 = jot a memo; 붙여 놓다 = stick and leave
Can you give me one Post-it?
장 counts the sheets; casual request
Don't stick Post-its on the monitor
I marked it with a Post-it
examples: 할 일을 포스트잇에 적어서 책상에 붙여요.
I write my to-dos on Post-its and stick them on my desk.
Everyday productivity habit; 할 일 = to-do
중요한 페이지마다 포스트잇을 붙여 두세요.
Put a Post-it on every important page.
마다 = every; 붙여 두다 = stick and keep
포스트잇이 떨어져서 메모가 사라졌어요.
The Post-it fell off and the note disappeared.
떨어지다 = fall off; common minor frustration
nuance: 포스트잇 is the everyday word even though it started as the 3M brand name, just like in English. The fully Korean term 접착 메모지 exists but sounds stiff and is rarely spoken; 포스트잇 is what you say at any office or stationery shop.
mistakes: Over-formalizing as 접착식 메모지 in casual speech when 포스트잇 is universal
Counting them with 개 instead of the natural 장 for sheets

usage: 묶다 = bind; 로 marks the tool
Can you take the clip off the documents?
Where did all the clips go?
Self-talk; clips always vanish in offices
A binder clip is better than a paper clip
examples: 영수증을 클립으로 묶어서 보관했어요.
I clipped the receipts together and kept them.
Practical filing; 보관하다 = to store
페이지가 많아서 클립 대신 스테이플러를 썼어요.
There were many pages, so I used a stapler instead of a clip.
대신 = instead of; links to 스테이플러
클립이 자석처럼 서로 달라붙어요.
The clips stick to each other like magnets.
달라붙다 = cling together; everyday observation
nuance: 클립 by itself means the small wire paper clip (also called 종이 클립). The larger black binder clip with metal arms is a different item, called 집게 or 더블클립, so specify when you need the strong one. Pair 클립 with 묶다 (to bind) or 끼우다 (to slip on).
mistakes: Using 클립 for the big black binder clip, which is 집게 / 더블클립
Saying 클립하다 as a verb; use 클립으로 묶다 or 클립을 끼우다

usage: I organized the documents in a folder
끼우다 = to insert; 두다 = leave it there
Give me one clear file, please
클리어파일 = the clear sleeve folder, very common
The file has gotten too thick
두꺼워지다 = become thick; full of papers
examples: 계약서를 파일에 넣어서 책장에 꽂아 뒀어요.
I put the contract in a file and shelved it.
Office filing; 꽂다 = to slot in
서류가 많으면 파일로 정리하는 게 편해요.
If you have lots of documents, organizing them in files is convenient.
-는 게 편하다 = it's convenient to
이 파일에는 영수증만 따로 모아요.
I keep only receipts together in this file.
따로 = separately; 모으다 = gather
nuance: Here 파일 means a physical document folder, but the same word also means a computer file, so context decides the meaning. The thin transparent sleeve folder most offices use is specifically a 클리어파일, while a ring binder is a 바인더.
mistakes: Assuming 파일 always means a computer file — physically it is a document folder
Calling the clear sleeve folder a 바인더, which is the thick ring binder

usage: Please scan it with the scanner
스캔하다 = to scan; 로 marks the tool
Can you scan the document for me?
연결이 안 되다 = fails to connect; tech complaint
examples: 계약서를 스캐너로 스캔해서 이메일로 보냈어요.
I scanned the contract and emailed it.
Standard office task chaining scan and email
요즘은 스캐너 대신 휴대폰 앱으로 스캔해요.
These days I scan with a phone app instead of a scanner.
대신 = instead; modern habit
스캐너에 종이가 걸려서 다시 넣었어요.
The paper jammed in the scanner, so I reloaded it.
걸리다 = jam; 넣다 = put in
nuance: 스캐너 is the device and 스캔하다 is the action verb; you can also use the casual 뜨다 ('서류를 떠 주세요') in spoken office Korean. Many offices now have a 복합기, an all-in-one that prints, copies, and scans, so people may say 복합기로 스캔하다 instead.
mistakes: Saying 스캐너하다 — the verb is 스캔하다 or 스캐너로 스캔하다
Confusing 스캐너 with 복사기; scanning makes a digital file, copying makes paper

usage: Please make a copy on the copier
복사하다 = to copy; 로 marks the machine
고장 나다 = to break down; frequent office news
examples: 회의 자료를 복사기로 30부 복사했어요.
I made 30 copies of the meeting materials on the copier.
부 counts copies/issues of documents
복사기에 종이가 걸려서 한참 헤맸어요.
The paper jammed in the copier and I struggled for a while.
걸리다 = jam; 헤매다 = flounder
복사기 토너가 떨어져서 흐리게 나와요.
The copier toner ran out, so it prints faintly.
토너 = toner; 흐리게 = faintly
nuance: 복사기 is the dedicated copy machine, but most modern offices actually have a 복합기 (all-in-one that copies, prints, and scans); people often still call it 복사기 out of habit. Count finished copies with the counter 부, as in 30부 (30 copies).
mistakes: Confusing 복사기 (copier, makes paper) with 프린터 (printer) or 스캐너 (scanner)
Counting copies with 개 instead of the natural 부

usage: The yellow highlighter is the most visible
Please underline it with a highlighter
줄 긋다 = to draw a line
examples: 시험 범위를 형광펜으로 칠해 놨어요.
I highlighted the exam scope.
칠하다 = to color in; 놓다 = keep it done
형광펜이 번져서 글씨가 안 보여요.
The highlighter smudged and I can't read the text.
번지다 = to bleed/smudge
계약서 핵심 조항에 형광펜으로 표시했어요.
I highlighted the key clauses in the contract.
조항 = clause; practical at work
nuance: 형광펜 literally means 'fluorescent pen' and is the standard word for a highlighter. The natural verbs are 칠하다 (to color over) or 표시하다 (to mark); you can also 줄을 긋다 (draw a line) with it, the same way you would underline.
mistakes: Calling it a 색연필 (colored pencil) — that is a different tool
Saying 형광펜하다; use 형광펜으로 칠하다 / 표시하다

usage: 자르다 = to cut; 로 marks the tool
Can you bring me the scissors?
가위질 = the act of cutting with scissors
안 들다 = not cut well/dull; standard phrase
examples: 테이프를 가위로 깔끔하게 잘랐어요.
I cut the tape cleanly with scissors.
Links to 테이프; 깔끔하게 = neatly
가위가 무뎌서 종이가 잘 안 잘려요.
The scissors are dull, so the paper doesn't cut well.
무디다 = dull; 잘리다 = get cut
문구점에서 사무용 가위를 하나 샀어요.
I bought a pair of office scissors at the stationery shop.
사무용 = for office use; 문구점 = stationery shop
nuance: 가위 is grammatically treated as singular in Korean, so '가위 하나' means one pair of scissors — there is no plural form like English 'a pair of.' The idiom for sharpness is 잘 들다 (cuts well) versus 안 들다 (dull), not the literal 날카롭다.
mistakes: Trying to pluralize like English; 가위 stays singular, count with 하나/한 개
Saying 가위가 날카롭지 않다 for 'dull' — natives say 가위가 안 들어요

usage: I'll jot it on a notepad
적어 두다 = write down and keep
Just give me one sheet of notepaper
Did you see the note on the desk?
I left the phone number on a notepad
examples: 전화 메시지를 메모지에 적어서 전해 줬어요.
I wrote the phone message on notepaper and passed it along.
Office message-taking; 전하다 = relay
메모지가 떨어져서 포스트잇에 적었어요.
The notepaper ran out, so I wrote on a Post-it.
Contrasts 메모지 vs 포스트잇; 떨어지다 = run out
책상마다 메모지와 볼펜을 놓아 두었어요.
I placed a notepad and pen on every desk.
마다 = on each; links to 볼펜
nuance: 메모지 is a small pad or loose sheets for quick notes, distinct from 노트 (a bound notebook) and 포스트잇 (the sticky kind). It pairs with the verb 적다 or 메모하다 (to jot down), and a single sheet is counted with 장.
mistakes: Confusing 메모지 (plain notepaper) with 포스트잇 (the self-stick kind)
Counting sheets with 개 instead of the natural 장
